title: Seek God and live — Amos 5
paragraphs: He was not asking for your performance.
He was calling for your return.
That verse lands like thunder because Amos was speaking to people who still looked religious on the outside. They had gatherings. Songs. Offerings. A form of worship.
But their hearts were far from God.
And the warning was sharp: You can be busy with church things and still be starving spiritually. You can know the language of faith and still be resisting the voice of God.
The command to seek God is also an invitation to be rescued.

Not “Seek Me and maybe I’ll tolerate you.”
Not “Seek Me once you clean yourself up.”
Not “Seek Me after you fix the mess.”

That means there is still mercy on the table.
Still time to return.
Still grace for the one who wandered, compromised, hid, got cold, got proud, got tired.

Real life is not found in success, applause, lust, money, or image.
Real life is found in God Himself.
And that life comes fully through Jesus Christ — the One who took our sin, carried our judgment, and rose again so dead hearts could live again.
So if your soul feels dry today, don’t just rearrange your habits.

Pray honestly.
Repent deeply.
Come to Christ openly.
